title: The missing group changes the rate
hook: Omit a low-rate group without changing any group’s own rate.

doesNotKnow: Audit who was omitted before interpreting an aggregate improvement.

misconception: A higher reported rate proves underlying outcomes improved.
objective: Audit who was omitted before interpreting an aggregate improvement.

claims.text: Statistical conclusions depend on how data were selected and measured.
David Spiegelhalter, The Art of Statistics (2019)
Both groups give {A}%; omitting group B gives {B}%. No unit’s stipulated rate improves; selection changes whose rates count.
Does it hold up? This exact aggregation shows selection sensitivity. It does not diagnose missingness in a real dataset.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: A report now includes only a high-rate subgroup. Does a higher average alone establish improvement?
recall.why: Changed inclusion can raise an aggregate with every subgroup rate unchanged.
